title: Canonical unbounded derived adjunction comparisons on arbitrary sheaf slices
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the chosen universe, with commutative coefficient rings and a structural map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $A$ be any sheaf of sets on the target, put $B=f^{-1}A$, and present the slices $\mathscr Y/A$ and $\mathscr X/B$ by the small element sites of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Write $R_{Y,A}$ and $R_{X,B}$ for the restricted rings and $r_Y,r_X$ for exact module restriction to these slices. There is a canonical ringed morphism $f_A:(\mathscr X/B,R_{X,B})\to(\mathscr Y/A,R_{Y,A})$ whose inverse image sends $(H\to A)$ to $(f^{-1}H\to B)$. Its ordinary module pullback and direct image satisfy $\sigma:f_A^*r_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Xf^*$ and $r_Yf_*\cong f_{A*}r_X$.
Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical K-flat pullbacks and K-injective direct images with their derived adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Exact restriction induces functors, denoted again by $r_X,r_Y$, on these derived categories. For every $M\in D(R_Y)$ and $E\in D(R_X)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$\theta_M:Lf_A^*r_YM\xrightarrow{\sim}r_XLf^*M,\qquad
\beta_E:r_YRf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{A*}r_XE.$$
Here $\theta$ is the canonical derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed slice square: on a K-flat complex $T$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] it is the image of $\sigma_T$ in the derived category, under the canonical representative identifications. Restriction of $T$ remains K-flat with flat terms. The map $\beta_E$ is represented, on a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], by the ordinary restriction/direct-image identity $r_Yf_*I\cong f_{A*}r_XI$; $r_XI$ is K-injective. Moreover $\beta$ is the adjunction exchange mate of $\theta$. In particular, for the canonical counits $\varepsilon$ of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $\varepsilon^A$ of $Lf_A^*\dashv Rf_{A*}$,
$$r_X(\varepsilon_E)\circ\theta_{Rf_*E}
=\varepsilon^A_{r_XE}\circ Lf_A^*(\beta_E).$$
No presentation of $f$ by a functor between the original sites, no flatness or invertibility of $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, and no boundedness assumption on the complexes is required.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; canonical square and module identities, extended to unbounded derived adjunctions by K-flat and K-injective representatives

proof.text: Use the element-site equivalences and exact restrictions of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Put $L=f^{-1}$ and $V=f_*$. The arrowwise functor $L_A:\mathscr Y/A\to\mathscr X/B$ preserves finite limits and has a right adjoint by [lem-sfb-left-exact-left-adjoint-slices]. Explicitly its right adjoint sends $p:H\to B$ to $A\times_{VB}VH\to A$, using $\eta_A:A\to VLA=VB$. Indeed, adjunction identifies a map $LK\to H$ over $B$ with a map $K\to VH$ whose composite to $VB$ is $\eta_A$ after $K\to A$; this is exactly a map into that pullback over $A$. Thus $L_A$ is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $f_A$. Since $L$ preserves products, $L_A(F\times A\to A)=(LF\times B\to B)$, naturally in $F$. This is the commutation isomorphism of the localization square.

Restrict the structural ring map $c:LR_Y\to R_X$ to $\mathscr X/B$. The last identity of step 1 identifies its domain with $L_A(R_{Y,A})$, so it gives $f_A$ its ringed structure and makes the square commute as a square of ringed topoi. Let $O=LR_Y$ on $\mathscr X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to the localization $j_B$ with coefficient ring $O$, to the $O$-modules $R_X$ and $LM$. Its structural ring map is an isomorphism, hence its module pullback is restriction. Together with step 1 this identifies
$$f_A^*r_YM=R_{X,B}\otimes_{r_XO}r_XLM\ \cong\ r_X(R_X\otimes_O LM)=r_Xf^*M.$$
Call this isomorphism $\sigma_M$. It preserves the scalar-extension insertion $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, since the tensor comparison is the canonical one. The module adjunctions used here are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

For an $R_X$-module $E$, restriction corresponds to the module object $E\times B\to B$. Step 1 gives
$$f_{A*}r_XE=A\times_{VB}V(E\times B)\cong A\times VE=r_Yf_*E.$$
Here $V(E\times B)\cong VE\times VB$: maps into either side are pairs of maps by the original adjunction. Addition is addition in $VE$ on each fibre. The scalar action is the action induced by $c$, restricted to that fibre, hence agrees on both sides by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Write $\delta:r_Yf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{A*}r_X$ for this natural identification. If $a:M\to f_*E$ has ordinary adjunct $\widetilde a:f^*M\to E$, then the adjunct of $\delta_E r_Ya$ is $r_X\widetilde a\,\sigma_M$. To check it, first apply the slice-adjoint pullback formula of step 1 to the underlying set-sheaf transpose: it is $r_X$ of the original transpose. The module adjunct extends that map from $1\otimes m$ by $s\otimes m\mapsto s\widetilde a(1\otimes m)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport]. Since $\sigma$ preserves these insertions, the two extensions are equal.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; Tags 03D3 and 03D7, underlying adjunction and scalar-extension transpose

proof.text: Both $r_X$ and $r_Y$ are exact and have exact additive left adjoints by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Therefore their termwise functors descend to unbounded derived categories, with the termwise representative identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. They preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], applied with the restriction as right adjoint and extension by zero as exact left adjoint. Independently, regard each restriction as module pullback along its ringed localization. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], it carries every K-flat complex with flat terms to a K-flat complex with flat terms. These arguments apply to the small element sites of step 1, so do not assume that $A$ was representable on an original site.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; derived.tex Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives

proof.text:
Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small source site. The canonical direct-image computations of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and step 4 give
$$r_YRf_*E\cong Q(r_Yf_*I)\xrightarrow{Q\delta_I}Q(f_{A*}r_XI)\cong Rf_{A*}r_XE.$$
Define this isomorphism to be $\beta_E$. It is independent of the representative and natural: every derived morphism between two K-injective representatives has a unique homotopy class of chain representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The naturality square of $\delta$ for such a chain map gives the square for $\beta$. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence by the same node; the additive functors and $\delta$ preserve this equivalence, which proves compatibility with changing representatives.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, K-injective computation; derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective

proof.text:
Use the mate bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] for the two canonical derived adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Define $\theta:Lf_A^*r_Y\to r_XLf^*$ to be the inverse mate of the natural transformation $\beta$ of step 5. Explicitly, with $\eta$ the global derived unit,
$$\theta_M=\varepsilon^A_{r_XLf^*M}\circ Lf_A^*(\beta_{Lf^*M})\circ Lf_A^*r_Y(\eta_M).$$
This gives a natural transformation. Its invertibility is not inferred merely from the invertibility of $\beta$; it will follow from its representative formula below.

Fix a flat-term K-flat complex $T$ on the target. Choose a K-injective resolution $i:f^*T\to I$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and let $a:T\to f_*I$ be its ordinary complex transpose under [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. The transpose of $\delta_I r_Ya$ under the slice module adjunction is, by the explicit identity of step 3,
$$h:f_A^*r_YT\xrightarrow{\sigma_T}r_Xf^*T\xrightarrow{r_Xi}r_XI.$$
Thus, writing only the chain map, $h=(r_Xi)\sigma_T$. This identity holds term by term, hence for complexes, because naturality of the ordinary adjunction makes the transposes commute with the differentials.

The K-flat computations of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], applied to $f$ and $f_A$, identify $Lf^*(QT)$ with $Q(f^*T)$ and $Lf_A^*r_Y(QT)$ with $Q(f_A^*r_YT)$; step 4 supplies the required K-flatness and flat terms of $r_YT$. The canonical derived adjunction is normalized by the ordinary chain transpose, as stated in [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization]: applied to $i$, the unit at $QT$, followed by the representative identification using $i$, is represented by $a$. Its hypotheses hold here by K-flat resolution existence [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], K-flat localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and K-injective existence. Consequently the three arrows defining $\theta_{QT}$ in step 6, followed by $Q(r_Xi)$ on its target, give $Q(h)$: the first arrow gives $r_Ya$, the second gives $\delta_I$, and the last takes the slice derived transpose, computed by the same normalization theorem since $r_XI$ is K-injective. By step 7 this is $Q(r_Xi)Q(\sigma_T)$. Cancel the isomorphism $Q(r_Xi)$, which is invertible by exactness of restriction. Thus $\theta_{QT}=Q(\sigma_T)$ under the specified representative identifications.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); derived.tex Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, canonical transpose normalization

proof.text:
Every $M$ is isomorphic to $QT$ for a flat-term K-flat $T$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Hence step 8 and naturality show that every $\theta_M$ is invertible, and identify it with the canonical pullback comparison induced by the ringed square, whose ordinary comparison was constructed in step 2. Step 5 already proves invertibility and the required representative formula for $\beta$. Finally, the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to $\theta$ and its mate $\beta$, gives
$$r_X(\varepsilon_E)\circ\theta_{Rf_*E}=\varepsilon^A_{r_XE}\circ Lf_A^*(\beta_E).$$
All constructions used the original geometric adjunction, small element sites and unbounded resolutions. None required a site functor presenting $f$, an invertible or flat structural ring map, or a bounded complex.
